summary: Farmers face shifting temperatures, changing rainfall, water shortages and declining soil health, which makes choosing a crop rotation harder every year. Field Shift is a decision-support tool that turns NASA Earth data into a simple answer: which three-year rotation fits my field? A farmer selects their region, soil type and water source, sets priorities (soil health, water saving, heat tolerance, income, resilience), and gets ranked rotations with five scores and plain-language reasons. A stress test shows how each plan holds up in a dry or hot year.
details:
Field Shift helps a farmer compare three-year crop rotations for their own field. The farmer picks a region, soil type and water source, then sets five priorities: soil health, water saving, heat tolerance, income and resilience. The tool scores every rotation on those five measures, ranks them, and explains each score in plain language (for example, legumes add nitrogen; growing one crop every year is flagged). A stress test re-scores the plan for a dry or hot year, and the farmer can compare their current rotation with the best match.

Benefits and impact: healthier soil, less water used and steadier harvests for smallholders, plus a simple tool for extension workers who advise them.

Tools: a single-page web app built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using a rule-based scoring model. This hackathon prototype runs on built-in sample climate profiles based on the kinds of measurements NASA provides (POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP, MODIS/HLS, GRACE-FO); the values are illustrative, and connecting the live NASA APIs is the next step.

Creativity: the tool starts from the farmer's priorities, not from the data, and gives reasons instead of only numbers. We considered low literacy, phone use and offline use. Field Shift supports a decision; it does not replace a local agronomist.

AI use: Claude (Anthropic) was used for research, writing, slide design and generating the prototype code.
